events.title: Fort Detroit Surrenders Without a Fight
events.description: During the War of 1812, American General William Hull surrendered Fort Detroit to a smaller British and Indigenous force led by Isaac Brock and Tecumseh. He did so without a real battle.
events.significance: The loss gave Britain control of the Michigan Territory for a time. It was an early humiliation for the United States in the war and made Brock and Tecumseh famous.

events.title: The Peterloo Massacre
events.description: Cavalry charged into a huge crowd at St Peter's Field in Manchester, England. The crowd had gathered to demand parliamentary reform. About 15 people were killed and hundreds were injured.
events.significance: Public outrage at the violence boosted the cause of political reform in Britain. It also led to a lasting debate about press freedom and the right to protest.

events.title: First Transatlantic Telegraph Message Between Leaders
events.description: US President James Buchanan and Queen Victoria exchanged greetings over the new transatlantic telegraph cable. This formally opened a link between North America and Europe.
events.significance: The cable failed within weeks. It still showed that instant communication across the ocean was possible, and a durable cable followed in 1866.

events.title: Kittinger's Record-Setting Leap From the Edge of Space
events.description: US Air Force Captain Joseph Kittinger jumped from a balloon at about 102,800 feet over New Mexico. His jump set records for the highest balloon ascent, highest parachute jump and fastest free fall.
events.significance: His jump gave researchers key data on high-altitude survival and escape. His records stood for decades, and the jump inspired later stratospheric jumps.

events.title: Elvis Presley Dies at Graceland
events.description: Elvis Presley, the singer known as the King of Rock and Roll, died at his Memphis home, Graceland, at age 42.
events.significance: His death shocked fans around the world. Graceland has since become one of the most visited homes in America, and his influence on popular music remains huge.
